newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-UDINESE FINED OVER SNOWBALL-THROWING FANS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UDINESE FINED OVER SNOWBALL-THROWING FANS.

text.p: Italian serie A club Udinese were fined six million lire ($3,600) on Wednesday after fans threw snowballs at a recent match.

Italy's serie A sporting judge also handed out a nine million lire ($5,400) fine to Napoli whose fans threw objects at a linesman, and a five million ($3,000) fine to Milan whose supporters hurled plastic bottles at a referee.
In serie B, Castel di Sangro and Venezia were given 20 million lire ($11,400) fines and Cesena 12 million ($7,200).

The judge reported that the Castel di Sangro fans had thrown a metal object which hit the referee on his right shoulder. Venezia were punished for supporters who spat at the referee while an assistant was hit by a flying orange.
The Cesena fans were reported to have let off firecrackers and thrown lighters and coins at the referee.
